prompt: Create a production game sprite atlas for SHELLBOUND, a top-down 2D puzzle action game about a tiny teal creature taking over discarded orange robot shells. Transparent background, six separated sprites in a strict 3 columns x 2 rows grid, equal square cells, each object centered in its own cell with at least 15 percent empty margin. Landscape 3:2 canvas. NO text, no labels, no borders, no background, no perspective floor, no dropped shadow outside the sprite. Consistent finely painted 2D game art, crisp chunky silhouettes, worn burnt-orange metal, dark navy recesses and subtle teal power lights, hand-painted premium indie game style. True overhead top-down camera. All chassis point RIGHT/east and look distinct when reduced to 64px. Row1 column1: tiny adorable luminous turquoise blob creature with two short antennae and large readable eyes, round compact silhouette. Row1 column2: heavy ram robot chassis with thick orange armor, side caterpillar treads, obvious triangular battering plow on right. Row1 column3: compact artillery chassis with paired tracks and a short oversized cannon pointing right. Row2 column1: magnetic chassis with large open horseshoe magnet facing right, distinct red and blue pole tips, small tracks. Row2 column2: agile round orange spider robot with four articulated legs on each side and teal central socket, wide horizontal silhouette. Row2 column3: large imposing industrial guardian boss, orange armored octagonal core, dark shutters around a glowing red eye, four massive mechanical legs. These are individual game assets, no characters riding on top of the machines. Keep clean transparent gaps between every sprite so six equal rectangular cuts isolate them.
preparation: Six equal atlas cuts, alpha bounds crop and normalization of nearly transparent texture padding. No gameplay images downloaded from third parties.
